title: My browser card game has secret recipes: fuse two cards, the AI invents a new one
author: thundergenie
selftext:
Moonfall is out, in the browser.

Every card pair is a secret recipe. Astral Sage + Cosmic Dragon = Constellation Wyrm, a card the game invented on the spot. Find an unknown recipe, price it, sell it to other players.

Matches play like a tabletop RPG: you choose what a card does, an LLM game master rules, then draws the match as manga.

What do you think?

[https://moonfall.io/go/rd](https://moonfall.io/go/rd)

comments.author: thundergenie
comments.body:
u/Fishy53 I reposted cause it an issue with the video. I can reply here to:

>I have bunches of questions, How does the llm create a card? Do you already have a list of combos and what they turn into? Also how are any of the affects handled if the AI is just generating them? Can a pair of cards create a different combo or is it the same each time?

  
The llm kinda just vibes when creating a card. After first discovery, subsequent fusions for all users find the same one. Only one card possible per pair. Effects just work because the cards don't have hard stats, more like a role-playing description.

replies.author: Fishy53
replies.body: I see so it's not having to create visual effects but just follow rules of the text?

replies.author: thundergenie
replies.body: Yes, for now. I do think it's possible to ask the llm to choose animations in realtime.

comments.author: Crunchfest3
comments.body: Since the first discovery already locks the recipe for everyone, I'd lean into showing buyers what they're paying for: reveal the resulting card, but hide the ingredients until purchase. With abilities described in prose, I'd also let the seller attach a replay of a turn where the card did something useful. That gives buyers a concrete example of how the GM interpreted it, without promising that it will work identically in every situation. Could turn the recipe market into a place for sharing tactics as well as combinations.

replies.author: thundergenie
replies.body: Good points! I think it could be tricky to show previews for fusions because then recipes could be brute forced. But I'll think about it. I'm really eager to see how the meta around this would develop, what feedback  community shares, and so on.

replies.author: thundergenie
replies.body: Not much. It should scale, but I'll be ready to act in case it gets there and there's some issue.

comments.author: PhysicalLevel4260
comments.body: Tried playing it on steam deck. Text scaling on a small screen needs work.

replies.author: thundergenie
replies.body: Interesting! There's always someone out there with a similar idea, huh? I was thinking, most of this was possible in some form even without AI. My biggest inspiration was Infinite Craft.
